questions.stem: Why can iron be extracted by reduction with carbon but sodium cannot?

options.text: Sodium is below carbon in the reactivity series
Sodium does not form an oxide compound
Iron is below carbon in the reactivity series, so carbon can reduce its oxide; sodium is above carbon, so it cannot
Iron is more reactive than carbon, so carbon can take its oxygen

questions.explanation: Iron is below carbon in the reactivity series, meaning carbon is more reactive than iron and can remove oxygen from iron oxide. Sodium is above carbon in the reactivity series, meaning sodium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot remove oxygen from sodium oxide. Electrolysis must be used for sodium instead.
